doc.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Dexter Gordon and other Keystone visitors
summary: Dexter Gordon stood out, as did Art Farmer and Clifford Jordan; he recalls Dexter as king of Europe when touring with Hutcherson.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah, a long list of people came through there. Any people stand out in your memory in particular?

Oh I mean some people stand out, you know even if I’d never worked with them but Dexter Gordon was one of them. He really was a bigger than life person. But a lot of great musicians. Art Farmer, there was a particularly nice evening with Art Farmer and Clifford Jordan, it was just — they were both wonderful people but what great players. And there’s so many different players.

Ebullient? You know one thing? I would go to Europe, me and Bobby — I worked with Bobby Hutcherson, mostly in the seventies, and we’d go to Europe a lot. And Dexter lived in Europe then. And he was the king of Europe, I am telling you. Everywhere Dexter played it’d be thousands of people. And he was just always real, and he’s just so tall and he was just so striking. And he would stay very, very polite and if he was going to play a song “Over the Rainbow” he’d say “Somewhere— Over the Rainbow — Way—” he’d say the first few lines of the song and especially if it was a ballad, then he had this big tone and all of a sudden, he would just knock you out. It was amazing. He was just like that. And I worked with him when he first came back and he didn’t have his regular band. And we went to Canada and different places. But so many, there were so many good musicians there. Everybody that came through there boy.
